elements.description:
Entities ranked by how often they appear together with a subject – strength in words and bars, a score, the share
of events, a count per source and when last seen – with each row opening its shared events.

properties.name: heading
properties.description: The heading, and the list's name

properties.name: window
properties.description: The time window the counts cover, shown in the header, e.g. "120-day window"

properties.name: sources
properties.description: The data sources, in the order their counts are shown

properties.name: entities
properties.description: The entities seen together with the subject

properties.name: events
properties.description: How many events the subject had in the window – the share's denominator

properties.name: eventUnit
properties.description: What an event is called after a number: "14 of 17 events"

properties.name: sort
properties.description: The order of the rows. Changed by the user unless a tc-sort-change listener calls preventDefault()

properties.name: selected
properties.description: The open row's id. Changed by the user unless a tc-selected-change listener calls preventDefault()

properties.name: thresholds
properties.description: The lowest shares, from 0 to 1, that count as Always together and Frequent; below Frequent is Occasional

properties.name: strengthLabels
properties.description: The strengths' names, merged over the defaults (Always together, Frequent, Occasional)

properties.name: locale
properties.description: The language for dates and numbers, e.g. "en-GB"; by default the browser's

properties.name: look
properties.description: Visual style: "standard" or "clean"; unset follows <tc-look-provider>, else "standard"

events.name: tc-selected-change
events.description: A row was opened or closed ({ selected, entity }: CoSelectedChange); cancelable – prevented, `selected` stays as it was

events.name: tc-sort-change
events.description: The sort was changed ({ sort }: CoSortChange); cancelable – prevented, `sort` stays as it was

functions.name: defaultCoStrengthLabels
functions.description: The strengths' names used when the page gives none

props.name: title
props.description: The heading, and the list's name

props.name: selected
props.description: The open row's id – controlled when given (null for none)

props.name: defaultSelected
props.description: The row open on mount when `selected` isn't controlled

props.name: onSelectedChange
props.description: A row was opened or closed; `entity` is the opened one

props.name: sort
props.description: The order of the rows – controlled when given

props.name: defaultSort
props.description: The order on mount when `sort` isn't controlled

changelog: **People & profiles:** - `tc-entity-timeline`: events by month, each with a category and a graded source, filtered by category. - `tc-travel-itinerary`: legs with mode, document, confidence and flags, grouped into journeys. - `tc-place-list`: places with type, status, coordinates and dates. - `tc-account-list`: masked IBAN-style accounts with a status and the page's own stats. - `tc-money-flow`: transfers between entities as bands sized by amount, with flag chips. - Entities' and transfers' flows are lit with a readout, and there's a table view. - `tc-co-occurrence`: entities ranked by the events they share with a subject. - Strength in words and bars, with counts per source. - `tc-evidence-list`: exhibits, each opening onto its chain of custody, with hash agreement. - `tc-asset-list`: grouped assets with masked identifiers and a status. - `tc-contact-channels`: emails, phone numbers, messaging and addresses. - Masked until shown, with role, last use and verification.

features.name: light-dark()
features.why: Every colour token is a light / dark pair; without it no colour token resolves.

features.name: color-mix()
features.why: Tints and washes mixed from the tokens.

features.name: Container size queries
features.why: Components adapt to the width they're given, not the window's.

features.name: :is() and :where()
features.why: Every rule is keyed on :where() so the page can override it.

features.name: adoptedStyleSheets
features.without: Each element type's CSS goes into one <style> element in <head> instead – it looks and works the same.

features.name: forced-colors media query
features.without: In a forced-colours mode the browser's own adjustments apply, without the components' fixes.
